claims.text: The local catalog and selected Bulbapedia snapshot bound this source slice from the CoroCoro February 1997 issue insert released January 15, 1997 through the CoroCoro November 1997 issue insert released October 15, 1997.
This release family is modeled as CoroCoro Comic issue inserts, not as a booster pack, deck, sealed set, tournament prize table, or complete magazine-object archive.
The local catalog models five source-pinned card identities across four issue-insert dates: Mew, Mewtwo, Surfing Pikachu, Imakuni?, and Flying Pikachu.
The source slice explicitly excludes later mail-in prize draws, JR East regular-stock Mew, Fan Book Mewtwo, ANA Flying Pikachu, official copy counts, and a complete CoroCoro 1997 promo census.

The local rows and selected card-page lines place different kinds of visual authority in the same tiny source slice: Ken Sugimori for Mew, Benimaru Itoh for Mewtwo, Toshinao Aoki for both Pikachu variants, and Takumi Akabane as a Photo. credit for Imakuni?.

CoroCoro early 1997 matters because it shows Pokemon cards traveling through magazine culture before they become only set numbers: mythical Mew, lab-myth Mewtwo, two impossible Pikachu stunts, and Imakuni? all arrive as media objects a reader could pull from an issue.

narrative.human_title: Magazine inserts before the world got tidy
narrative.why_it_matters: CoroCoro early 1997 feels like Pokemon still discovering where a card could live. Mew comes out of the magazine as a glossy rumor you can hold. Mewtwo follows like the laboratory shadow. Then September turns strange and perfect: Surfing Pikachu and Imakuni? on the same insert, mascot gag beside human performance. Flying Pikachu closes the slice by making the mascot impossible again. For an agent, the charm and the danger are the same thing: each card is famous enough to be remembered loosely, but only useful when the exact magazine route stays attached.
